paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Having everything is not the same as enjoying anything. The Teacher, son of David and king in Jerusalem, shows us a man with riches, wealth and honor who "lacks nothing his heart desires," yet God does not allow him to enjoy them (Ecclesiastes 6:2). Enjoying what we have is a gift from God, and no amount of stuff, years or family can stand in for it (Ecclesiastes 5:19; 6:3).

So why do we keep chasing more? The Teacher says "All a man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied" (Ecclesiastes 6:7). He says "Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire" (Ecclesiastes 6:9). Think of it like a batch already on my cooling rack beating the ten batches I keep daydreaming about. Chasing the next thing is "a pursuit of the wind" (Ecclesiastes 6:9).

The Teacher also reminds us that we can't see the whole road. He asks, "who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow?" (Ecclesiastes 6:12). That doesn't mean give up, baker. It means hold your plans loosely and receive today's cookie with thanks, because every good day is a gift from God. I'm still learning that one myself, and I'll keep learning it beside you.
